gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the 4-bay candidates cost today. TerraMaster's own store now sells the F4-424 Pro, which ChatGPT called its best compact pick, for $759.99. That is $130 more than the F4-425 Pro that replaces it ($629.99, dual 5GbE, 3× M.2) and $140 more than UGREEN's DXP4800 Plus ($619.99), which has a 10GbE port.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages and our own page. The NASCompares F4-424 Pro guide gives an old range of '$599 to $699' and names no successor. needtoknowit.com.au gives only an AUD market price (~$1,118) for the DXP4800 Pro and no US prices. Our own page still lists the F4-424 Pro at $699.99, which is out of date. ChatGPT's cards showed the F4-425 Pro at $559.99 (Newegg), which matches cnx-software's report of a time-limited 20% store promotion on the N305 version. None of these pages lines up today's maker-store prices across UGREEN, TerraMaster and QNAP, or shows that the older F4-424 Pro now costs more than both newer 4-bay boxes.
decides: This confirms the DXP4800 Plus as the 4-bay pick and argues against the F4-424 Pro. For $619.99 the DXP4800 Plus adds 10GbE and comes with UGREEN's documented position that installing another OS leaves the warranty intact. The F4-424 Pro costs $140 more and has only 2× 2.5GbE. The F4-425 Pro ($629.99) is the closest rival on price, but I found no Unraid or TrueNAS install report for it. For 6 and 8 bays, the DXP6800 Pro ($1,099.99) costs $99 less than QNAP's TS-873A-8G ($1,199). The QNAP has 2× 2.5GbE against the UGREEN's 2× 10GbE and ships with a 2–4 week lead time.
